appendBlocks.title: Level-up → incremental file ingestion
appendBlocks.text: Chapter 12 shows why re-running `spark.read` over a folder duplicates data, how COPY INTO remembers loaded files, and how Auto Loader with `.trigger(availableNow=True)` gives a scheduled job that is batch-like *and* incremental. (see Chapter 12: Data Ingestion: Files, COPY INTO & Auto Loader.)

appendExercises.q: A scheduled Auto Loader job using `.trigger(availableNow=True)` is an example of batch-like scheduling with incremental processing.
appendExercises.explain: AvailableNow processes all new files available at start, then stops — run hourly from a Job it behaves like batch, but the checkpoint makes each run touch only new files. Batch vs streaming describes timing; incremental describes how much work is redone.

appendFlashcards.q: Plain spark.read over the whole folder every day — incremental?
appendFlashcards.a: No: it re-reads every file each run (duplicates on append). Use COPY INTO or Auto Loader for file-level incremental loads.

appendBlocks.title: Level-up → checkpoints in Auto Loader
appendBlocks.text: Auto Loader has TWO state locations: `checkpointLocation` (progress — which files are done) and `cloudFiles.schemaLocation` (the inferred schema and its history). Chapter 12 adds the incident playbooks: checkpoint deleted, shared between streams, or kept after changing the source path. (see Chapter 12: Data Ingestion: Files, COPY INTO & Auto Loader.)

appendExercises.q: In an Auto Loader stream, which location remembers **which files have already been processed**?
why: Auto Loader's file progress is in the checkpoint.
appendExercises.explain: Progress lives in the streaming checkpoint (`checkpointLocation` on the write). `cloudFiles.schemaLocation` stores the inferred schema and its evolution — not progress. A `/tmp` path is ephemeral and would lose everything when compute terminates.

appendFlashcards.a: Checkpoint = how far the stream got (processed files/state). schemaLocation = what shape the data has (schema + history).

appendBlocks.title: Level-up → schema evolution at ingestion time
appendBlocks.text: Auto Loader makes the 'evolve vs enforce' decision concrete with `cloudFiles.schemaEvolutionMode` (addNewColumns / rescue / failOnNewColumns / none) and a `_rescued_data` column that keeps values that don't fit. Its default deliberately stops the stream on a new column, then continues with the new schema after restart. (see Chapter 12: Data Ingestion: Files, COPY INTO & Auto Loader.)

appendExercises.q: With Auto Loader's default schema evolution (schema inferred, addNewColumns), a new column in a source file stops the stream; after a restart the column is part of the schema.
appendExercises.explain: Stopping is a deliberate control point: the new schema is recorded in schemaLocation, and a restart (e.g. via Job retries) continues with it. It's 'enforcement + an explicit evolution policy', not silent mutation.

appendBlocks.title: Level-up → a production Bronze table
appendBlocks.text: A robust Bronze row = source fields (often kept as STRING) + `_source_file` + `_ingested_at` + `_rescued_data`; rows with rescued content go to a quarantine table, and business-key dedup/MERGE happens in Silver. (see Chapter 12: Data Ingestion: Files, COPY INTO & Auto Loader.)

appendExercises.q: Auto Loader infers JSON/CSV columns as STRING by default. Why is that often a *good* fit for Bronze?
options: It preserves odd values like "unknown" so Silver can validate and cast
Delta cannot store DOUBLE in Bronze
Unity Catalog forbids typed Bronze tables
why: Strings are usually slower for math.
appendExercises.explain: Bronze should preserve the source. If tomorrow `amount` arrives as "unknown", a STRING column keeps it; a DOUBLE column would fail or push it to rescued data. Silver then validates and casts. The other options are false claims.

appendBlocks.title: Level-up → the 8-step 'new files, no rows' chain
appendBlocks.text: For file ingestion the source→Bronze boundary splits into eight checks: files exist → path matches → extension/format → discovered → checkpoint already processed → parsing → schema → sink. Chapter 12 turns it into a playbook with scenarios. (see Chapter 12: Data Ingestion: Files, COPY INTO & Auto Loader.)

appendExercises.q: If the Auto Loader query progress shows the new files were read but 0 rows reached Bronze, the stream's load path is the most likely problem.
appendExercises.explain: If files were read, discovery (and therefore the path) worked. The break is later in the chain: parsing (format/extension mismatch, rescued or corrupt records), a schema-change stop, or the sink write.

appendBlocks.title: Level-up → file idempotency vs business-key idempotency
appendBlocks.text: Exactly-once file ingestion (Auto Loader/COPY INTO) never guarantees one row per order_id: two different files can carry the same key. First ask *same file twice or two different files?* — the answer tells you whether to fix ingestion state or Silver's MERGE. (see Chapter 12: Data Ingestion: Files, COPY INTO & Auto Loader.)

appendExercises.q: Silver shows order_id 100 twice. A colleague blames Auto Loader.

steps.prompt: The two Bronze rows have different `_source_file` values. What does that tell you?

options.text: Auto Loader processed two distinct files once each; the duplicate comes from the source
Auto Loader ingested the same file twice

options.fb: A reset re-ingests the SAME files — same `_source_file`, new `_ingested_at`.

options.text: Silver: dedupe by order_id and MERGE on the business key
Delete one of the source files

appendBlocks.title: Level-up → idempotent file loads
appendBlocks.text: COPY INTO is idempotent per *file*: re-runs skip already-loaded files — even if a file's content was later changed. Only `COPY_OPTIONS ('force' = 'true')` reloads, and then you own the duplicates. (see Chapter 12: Data Ingestion: Files, COPY INTO & Auto Loader.)

appendExercises.q: Upstream overwrote an already-loaded `orders_0928.csv` with corrected amounts. What does the next normal COPY INTO run do with it?
options: Skips it — it was already loaded
Reloads it because the content changed
why: COPY INTO never deletes old rows.
appendExercises.explain: COPY INTO tracks loaded file identities; a modified file with an already-loaded identity is skipped. Corrections should arrive as new files; a deliberate reload needs FILES + force and a cleanup of the old rows.

appendBlocks.title: Level-up → mergeSchema in COPY INTO
appendBlocks.text: COPY INTO has two different mergeSchema switches: `FORMAT_OPTIONS ('mergeSchema'='true')` merges the schemas of the source files, `COPY_OPTIONS ('mergeSchema'='true')` evolves the target Delta table. (see Chapter 12: Data Ingestion: Files, COPY INTO & Auto Loader.)

appendExercises.q: Complete COPY INTO so that new source columns are merged across files AND added to the target table.
appendExercises.text:
COPY INTO ecommerce.bronze.orders_raw
FROM '/path/'
FILEFORMAT = CSV
[[FORMAT_OPTIONS]] ('header' = 'true', 'mergeSchema' = 'true')
[[COPY_OPTIONS]] ('mergeSchema' = 'true');
appendExercises.explain: FORMAT_OPTIONS = how the source files are read (merge their schemas); COPY_OPTIONS = how the target is loaded (evolve its schema). With only one of them the new column may not reach the table.

appendBlocks.title: Level-up → the full Phase 4
appendBlocks.text: Chapter 12 is the complete Phase 4: CSV options and modes, StructType/DDL schemas, `_metadata.file_path`, every COPY INTO clause (PATTERN, FILES, VALIDATE, transforms, two mergeSchemas), Auto Loader internals, 13 debugging playbooks and the Big Test. (see Chapter 12: Data Ingestion: Files, COPY INTO & Auto Loader.)

appendExercises.q: The folder contains `orders_001.csv`, `orders_002.csv`, `customers_001.csv`. This COPY INTO loads nothing. Which line?
appendExercises.explain: COPY INTO's PATTERN is a **glob**, not a regex. `'orders_.*[.]csv'` would need a literal dot after `orders_`; `'orders_*.csv'` matches the order files.

appendExercises.q: Because Auto Loader ingests each file exactly once (with an intact checkpoint), the Bronze table cannot contain two rows with the same order_id.
appendExercises.explain: Exactly-once is about files. Two distinct files (an upstream retry or resend) can carry the same order_id, and both are correctly ingested once. Business-key dedup/MERGE belongs in Silver.

appendFlashcards.q: Auto Loader's default sample for initial schema inference?
appendFlashcards.a: Up to 50 GB or 1000 files, whichever is reached first.

appendBlocks.title: Level-up → read_files before Lakeflow
appendBlocks.text: `read_files(path, format => ..., schema => ...)` also works as a plain SQL reader for ad-hoc exploration; with `STREAM` inside a streaming table it runs Auto Loader, so checkpoints, string inference, schema evolution and `_rescued_data` all apply. (see Chapter 12: Data Ingestion: Files, COPY INTO & Auto Loader.)
